title: Daikyu
extract:
The Daikyu is an asymmetrical bow of  Tenno design and origin. It has larger damage, status chance and increased Projectile Speed compared to the other bows, as well as high critical chance, but takes longer to fully draw and cannot be released early for decreased damage.

Characteristics
This weapon primarily deals  Puncture damage.
Guaranteed  Impact proc.
Can fully benefit of  Internal Bleeding.
Charged shots have an innate 3 meter punch through, the highest of all bows.
As it can only be fired when fully charged, shots will always have the punch through.
On kill, bodies will follow the arrow that killed them, damaging anyone in their path and pinning the corpse to walls.
Medium-to-high zoom level when aiming.
Can equip the bow-exclusive  Thunderbolt mod, and the Daikyu-exclusive  Spring-Loaded Broadhead and  Amalgam Daikyu Target Acquired mods.
Fire rate mods apply double their bonuses.
Innate  polarity.
Advantages over other Primary  Bow weapons (excluding modular weapons):

Highest shot base damage of all bows. (without counting the AOE effect of  Proboscis Cernos, Kuva Bramma, and  Lenz)
Second highest status chance of all bows, behind  Mutalist Cernos.
Second fastest Projectile Speed of all primary weapons, behind  Lanka.
Fastest Projectile Speed of all bows.
Arrows have low arc due to flight speed.
Charged Shot (wiki attack index 1)
Very high burst DPS (938)
Very high sustained DPS (586.25)
Very high damage per shot (938)
Very high total damage (700)
Very high ammo pickup (15)
Very high ammo max (72)
Very high fire rate (1.00 attacks/sec)
High status chance (46.00%)
High disposition (●●●●○ (1.30x))
Disadvantages over other Primary  Bow weapons (excluding modular weapons):

Second slowest charge speed of all bows, after  Lenz.
Cannot be fired at partial charge.
Arrows have travel time with slight arcing.
Charged Shot (wiki attack index 1)
Below average crit chance (34.00%)
Low reload speed (0.60 s)
Very low crit multiplier (2.00x)

Acquisition
The Daikyu's blueprint can be researched from the Tenno Lab in the dojo.

This weapon can be sold for  7,500.

Notes
The Daikyu does not have a quick fire option, nor can it be fired at partial charge - it must be fully charged before it can be fired.
The weapon's charge, both in its draw phase and its hold phase, can be cancelled by performing actions that will break normal weapon charges, such as pressing reload, rolling, or switching to another weapon.
The Daikyu reportedly does not benefit from multiplicative gun CO from Galvanized Aptitude. Instead, it acts the same as damage mods like Serration, Heavy Caliber, or gun Arcanes like Primary Merciless.

Tips
This weapon is perfect for  Internal Bleeding: with the guaranteed  Impact proc and slow fire rate, each arrow has 70% chance to apply bleed.
With  Internal Bleeding +  Vile Acceleration +  Critical Delay, the weapon has guaranteed crit (120%), a fast charge time (0.42s), and is still just above the threshold to have 70% proc rate from Internal Bleeding.
The increased Projectile Speed and subsequent low arc makes it much easier to achieve headshots and hit enemies at very long ranges.
 Speed Trigger, ( Primed)  Shred,  Vigilante Fervor and  Vile Acceleration can be used individually or in combination to speed up the Daikyu's draw speed.

Trivia
The daikyū (大弓) is one of two variants of the Japanese asymmetrical yumi bow. Read as "big bow" or "Longbow", the daikyū is the larger variant to the smaller hankyū (半弓; lit. "half bow").
The mechanics of this bow appear to be heavily based on the principles of Kyūdō, the practice of Japanese archery. By taking one's time and adopting proper shooting posture and form, the arrow is assured to hit its mark.
The Codex description mentions great strength required to draw the Daikyu, which may refer to its prolonged drawing time.
The Daikyu was the first bow that has a completely compact, collapsible form when holstered. It folds into three pieces: its two arms and the grip, creating a U-shape as the arms point upward on the player's back. The  Lenz would follow as the second, folding in a similar manner.
